candidate_findings.title: Historical-mode contract is simultaneously accepted and declared absent
candidate_findings.claim: The owner section is labeled canonical live text and contains an accepted Historical Run Mode PlanUnit, yet preserved bullets say there is no clear or explicit mode contract. The document does not mark those assertions as retired lineage or resolve their status.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementers and validators cannot determine whether the accepted state model or the unresolved recommendation language is binding, allowing incompatible page behavior to pass review.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Provide one authoritative historical-mode state machine and explicitly retire or quarantine contradictory source-lineage bullets from canonical requirements.

candidate_findings.title: Nullable focus identity and concurrent active-run lifecycle are undefined
candidate_findings.claim: Both run IDs are expressed as optional, while live mode is defined by equality without a non-null guard. The singular active_run_id model also lacks behavior for zero or multiple active/background runs, and the text explicitly leaves background-run interaction unclear.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A null-equals-null implementation can misclassify an empty project as live, while run start, completion, pause, resume, or concurrent background activity can silently move or corrupt the user's persisted focus.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define non-null invariants, zero/one/many active-run representation, default selection, all focus transitions, persistence revisioning, event-versus-navigation ordering, and behavior when a focused run is removed or becomes active.

evidence_refs.excerpt: `active_run_id?` names live runtime truth, while `focused_run_id?` and `focus_mode = live | historical` name the page selection
`focus_mode = live` when `focused_run_id == active_run_id`, and `focus_mode = historical` when the user inspects a non-active run.
focus_mode is live only when focused_run_id equals active_run_id

candidate_findings.title: Stale-projection disclosure has no deterministic action gate
candidate_findings.claim: The document requires stale/degraded disclosure but uses permissive language that live affordances may gate and should disclose. It provides no trust-state enumeration, freshness boundary, source precedence, or command allow/deny matrix.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A UI can accurately display a stale warning while still enabling a blocked approval, recovery, or generation action against obsolete runtime truth.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define authoritative trust states, freshness and provenance fields, transition triggers, non-bypassable per-command gates, refresh/recovery behavior, disabled reasons, and audit records for attempted stale actions.

candidate_findings.title: Shared destination payload has behavior but no wire contract
candidate_findings.claim: The same payload must serve search, command palette, recovery, resume, artifact, preview, and cross-surface navigation, but the capsule specifies neither a required schema/version nor validation, project/run binding, target-existence, expiry, authorization, replay, or stale-generation behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Approximate, stale, cross-project, or forged destinations can select the wrong run or object, leak inaccessible context, or route an action-adjacent flow against an unintended target.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify a versioned tagged-union payload with required identity scopes, canonical serialization, generation and blocked-sequence guards, destination reauthorization, expiry/replay rules, rejection codes, and round-trip fixtures.

candidate_findings.title: Node selection does not deterministically select an attempt
candidate_findings.claim: The inspector promises requested-versus-effective, provider, usage, retry, and execution details after a node click, while the persistent runtime record is per attempt and only for attempts that resolved provider routing. No rule selects among retries or represents queued, cancelled, or pre-routing failures.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A node with multiple attempts can display cost, provider, status, evidence, or recovery controls from the wrong attempt and present that composite as node truth.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define node-to-attempt cardinality, default and explicit attempt selection, comparison behavior, late-arrival ordering, partial/unresolved field states, and an invariant that every displayed fact names its attempt source.

candidate_findings.title: Graph-patch generation transitions lack atomicity and conflict semantics
candidate_findings.claim: The graph must span generations and patch application is described both as a hard gate and as something that should likely be hard-gated, but there is no authoritative transition owner, generation precondition, concurrent-patch ordering, idempotency key, cancellation boundary, rollback, or lineage invariant.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent or retried patch application can fork from stale generation state, duplicate generations, mislabel the current generation, or lose rejoin lineage while the GUI still renders a coherent-looking graph.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define request, approval, apply, reject, cancel, fail, recover, and supersede states; expected-generation compare-and-swap; idempotency; conflict resolution; immutable lineage edges; and deterministic current-generation selection.

candidate_findings.title: Safe-point restore-and-retry lacks an execution lifecycle
candidate_findings.claim: Exact worktree and baseline targeting is required, but the consumer contract does not require last-moment HEAD revalidation, locking, authorization, confirmation, idempotency, partial-failure receipts, cancellation semantics, or recovery after restore succeeds and retry fails.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A delayed or repeated command can overwrite newer worktree state, launch duplicate retries, or leave the UI claiming recovery without distinguishing restore and retry outcomes.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Require target revision preconditions, exclusive mutation lease, policy check, confirmation rules, idempotency key, two-phase outcome receipts, cancellation points, retry policy, and explicit partial-state rendering.

candidate_findings.title: Host access pivots are not bound to focused historical identity
candidate_findings.claim: Canonical URLs are convenience bindings for the active selected or checked-out instance, while historical mode may retain a different focused run. The capsule does not state which run and host-assignment revision Open App or Open Container targets, nor how URL schemes, redirects, changed ports, or permission denial are handled.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: From a historical graph, a user can believe they are opening that run's instance while the action reaches the current checked-out instance or an unsafe stale address.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Bind each pivot to focused_run_id, node, attempt, host_assignment_id, and observed revision; define historical-safe behavior, scheme and destination validation, redirect policy, expiry recheck, destination authorization, confirmation, audit, and deterministic refusal reasons.

candidate_findings.title: Concern references have no canonical lifecycle or nomination contract
candidate_findings.claim: Run Graph is required to expose concern-related references, while merge and supersession remain discussion-only, acknowledgement is explicitly non-resolution, and the document still instructs authors to define how findings become concerns. Creation, deduplication, ownership, transition authority, resolution, reopening, and propagation are not binding here.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The graph can show durable-looking concern state that different consumers create, dismiss, merge, or resolve inconsistently, losing provenance or treating noise suppression as remediation.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Name the concern owner and canonical schema; define nomination and deduplication; allowed state transitions and actors; acknowledgement, dismissal, resolution, reopening, supersession, and merge semantics; idempotency; lineage propagation; and deterministic tests.

candidate_findings.title: Large-graph behavior has mechanisms but no measurable limits
candidate_findings.claim: The document names culling, caching, throttling, virtualization, and thousands of nodes without defining maximum nodes, edges, generations, update throughput, latency, frame, memory, cache invalidation, backpressure, or overload-degradation requirements.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations can satisfy the named mechanisms yet freeze, drop state transitions, evict selected lineage, or render stale overlays under realistic load.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define supported size and event-rate envelopes, interaction and render budgets, memory caps, update-coalescing invariants, cache keys and invalidation, backpressure, overload UI, selection preservation, and benchmark fixtures.
